name: Kennedia prostrata
description: A scrambling groundcover or restrained climber with grey-green leaves in threes and scarlet pea flowers from late winter into spring. It spills well over walls and from hanging baskets.
care_note: In a long dry spell it may die back to its roots and shoot again when rain returns.

name: Kennedia nigricans
description: A vigorous Western Australian climber with dark green leaves and unusual black and yellow pea flowers. It covers a fence quickly and can also be grown as a groundcover.
pruning: Trim after flowering if the plant needs tidying.

name: Billardiera scandens
description: A light twining climber with bell-shaped flowers in spring, followed by fleshy fruits with a sweet pulp. It scrambles through shrubs without smothering them, and its flowers feed honeyeaters.

name: Viola banksii
description: A spreading groundcover with kidney-shaped leaves and purple and white flowers through the warmer months. It is the plant long sold as Viola hederacea, and it can cover a large area in moist shade.
care_note: It can overrun slow-growing prostrate plants nearby.

name: Rhodanthe anthemoides
description: A small everlasting daisy with narrow grey-green leaves and white papery flower heads over a long season. Cultivars such as 'Paper Cascade' have purple buds and suit pots and rockeries.
pruning: Cut back after flowering to keep the plant tidy.

name: Lechenaultia biloba
description: A small Western Australian wildflower with narrow leaves and vivid blue flowers, sometimes pale blue or white, in winter and spring.
care_note: It usually lives four to six years. In humid eastern gardens it does best in a pot of free-draining mix.

name: Grevillea sericea
description: A shrub from the New South Wales central coast with pink spider flowers from autumn to spring. Native bees and honey bees find the flowers very attractive.
pruning: It responds well to pruning for a more compact shape.

name: Commelina cyanea
description: A trailing groundcover with fleshy stems, narrow leaves and bright blue flowers from spring to autumn that attract native bees. It grows fast in warm, wet weather and dies back in cool, dry months.
care_note: It can colonise bare ground and smother small plants, so please keep an eye on where it spreads. It looks like the weed trad, which has white flowers.

name: Dichondra repens
description: A low creeping groundcover with small kidney-shaped leaves that spreads by runners. It makes a soft lawn substitute where there is little foot traffic.
care_note: In full sun it needs water in dry spells.

name: Scaevola albida
description: A low, spreading fan-flower covered in small white, blue or mauve flowers for most of the year. Cultivars such as 'Mauve Carpet' make a dense mat.

name: Grevillea 'Poorinda Royal Mantle'
description: A prostrate grevillea with toothed leaves, coppery new growth and red toothbrush flowers from winter to late spring, with some flowers all year. It can cover a bank up to 6 metres across and gives bees nectar for most of the year.

name: Grevillea 'Moonlight'
description: A tall, tough grevillea that flowers all year and makes a good informal screen or hedge. Its flower heads feed nectar-eating birds and last well when cut.
pruning: Flowers form at the ends of the branches, so cut each flowered shoot back behind the spent flower heads.

name: Grevillea 'Coconut Ice'
description: A medium grevillea like 'Robyn Gordon', with large pink and cream flower spikes through most of the year. Its slightly prickly leaves give small birds a safe place to nest.

name: Grevillea 'Peaches and Cream'
description: A spreading grevillea like 'Robyn Gordon', with flower spikes that open yellow and turn shades of pink and orange from spring to autumn.

name: Grevillea 'Bronze Rambler'
description: A fast, dense groundcover grevillea with deeply divided bronze-red leaves and deep purple-red toothbrush flowers through the year. It smothers weeds and shelters frogs, lizards and small birds.

name: Lomandra confertifolia
description: A compact mat-rush with narrow leaves, sold in selections such as 'Little Con' for borders, pots and mass planting. If harsh weather damages the leaves, it can be cut back hard and will shoot again.

name: Lomandra filiformis
description: A fine-leaved mat-rush from dry forests on sandy or rocky soils. Selections such as 'Savanna Blue' have blue-grey leaves and suit small gardens and pots.

name: Conostylis candicans
description: A compact tuft of silver-grey, grass-like leaves with golden-yellow balls of flowers in spring. It is a relative of the kangaroo paws and suits a sunny pot or border.
pruning: Trim off the old flower stems and leaves after flowering.

name: Anigozanthos manglesii
description: The floral emblem of Western Australia, with velvety green flowers on bright red stems from late winter into summer.
care_note: It can be short-lived where rain or humidity is high. A raised bed or a large pot helps it last.

name: Xanthorrhoea preissii
description: A slow-growing, long-lived grass tree from Western Australia with a dark trunk, a tuft of grassy leaves and cream flowers on a tall spike every few years.
care_note: On clay soil, please plant it in a raised bed to prevent root rot. Water it regularly while it settles in, but do not overwater.

name: Arthropodium milleflorum
description: A grass-like lily with nodding, vanilla-scented white to pale pink or blue flowers from late spring into summer. It grows from edible tubers and dies back in dry times.
care_note: Please mark where it grows, so it is not weeded out while it is dormant.

name: Thelionema caespitosum
description: A tufted lily with narrow leaves and starry blue, white or yellow flowers in spring and summer. It suits rockeries, borders and pots.
pruning: Remove spent flower stems after flowering.

name: Doryanthes palmeri
description: A giant rosette of sword-shaped leaves with a tall flower head in spring. It makes a striking feature plant and grows well in a large container.
pruning: Cut off old flower heads and remove dead leaves in autumn.

name: Correa alba
description: A tough coastal shrub with grey, felty leaves and open, star-shaped white flowers, mainly in autumn and winter. It resists salt spray and suits seaside gardens.

name: Correa pulchella
description: A small correa from south-east South Australia, from prostrate to about a metre tall, with orange to red bell flowers from winter to early spring. Honeyeaters feed on its nectar.
care_note: It does best where summers are dry and can be short-lived in humid areas. It grows naturally on alkaline soil, so acid soil may need lime or dolomite.

name: Correa glabra
description: An upright correa from rocky woodland that flowers through autumn, winter and spring. It tolerates frost and drought, and golden-leaved forms such as 'Barossa Gold' suit pots and low hedges.

name: Boronia megastigma
description: A small Western Australian shrub with intensely fragrant flowers in spring, long grown for cut flowers. It is often short-lived, so many gardeners keep it in a pot.
pruning: Prune straight after flowering.
care_note: It needs well-drained, slightly acid soil, shelter from wind and a cool, mulched root run. Please keep the soil moist but not wet.

name: Boronia pinnata
description: A small shrub with aromatic, feathery leaves and starry pink flowers, sometimes white, at their best in spring.
pruning: Trim back by about a fifth after flowering.
care_note: It needs good drainage and a cool root run, such as a spot in a rockery.

name: Crowea saligna
description: A small shrub with willow-like leaves and large pink star flowers from late summer to mid-winter.
care_note: It does best in part shade. In full sun it needs extra water in dry spells, and mulch keeps its roots cool.

name: Crowea exalata
description: A small, variable crowea, from almost prostrate to about a metre high, with aromatic leaves and pink, sometimes white, star flowers from late summer to mid-winter. Native bees and butterflies visit them.

name: Prostanthera ovalifolia
description: The most widely grown mint bush, smothered in purple or mauve flowers in spring. Its leaves give off a strong minty scent when brushed or wet with rain.
fertiliser_note: Feed once a year after flowering. Mint bushes are less sensitive to phosphorus than many natives.
pruning: Prune back by about a third each year after flowering to keep it bushy.
care_note: It likes a moist, well-drained spot with some shelter from summer sun, and it wilts quickly when dry. It can die if the soil stays waterlogged.

name: Prostanthera rotundifolia
description: A compact mint bush with small, round, aromatic leaves and prolific purple flowers, sometimes pink, in spring.
fertiliser_note: Feed once a year after flowering. Mint bushes are less sensitive to phosphorus than many natives.
care_note: It likes a moist, well-drained spot with some shelter from summer sun, and it wilts quickly when dry.

name: Banksia robur
description: A striking banksia with large, stiff, toothed leaves, felty brown new growth and bluish-green flower spikes that age to yellow-green. It grows naturally in damp sandy ground but adapts to most soils.
care_note: It flowers best in full sun. Young plants may need protection from frost.

name: Banksia serrata
description: A gnarled banksia with warty bark, saw-toothed leaves and large silver-yellow flower spikes full of nectar in summer and autumn. It is a small tree in sheltered forest and a shrub on the coast, and a prostrate form called 'Pygmy Possum' makes a groundcover.

name: Banksia aemula
description: A gnarled coastal banksia with serrated leaves and large green-yellow flower spikes in autumn. It grows on sandy heaths between Sydney and Bundaberg.

name: Banksia menziesii
description: A large shrub or small tree with acorn-shaped flower spikes, mostly red or orange-brown, in autumn and winter. Honeyeaters feed on them, and they are grown as cut flowers.
care_note: It needs very good drainage. On the humid east coast it is hard to keep, because it is prone to dieback from a soil-borne disease.

name: Isopogon anemonifolius
description: A small shrub with finely lobed leaves and round golden flower heads in spring, followed by drumstick-like fruits. Honeyeaters and wrens visit it.

name: Telopea speciosissima
description: The floral emblem of New South Wales: a tall shrub with large, tight red flower heads from mid-spring to early summer that feed honeyeaters and make long-lasting cut flowers.
care_note: It needs excellent drainage but steady moisture, and it will not thrive in heavy shade or under large trees.

name: Calytrix tetragona
description: A small shrub with tiny, spicy-scented leaves and masses of starry white to pink flowers in spring, followed by decorative calyces. Both last well as cut flowers.
care_note: It needs well-drained soil, ideally a raised bed.

name: Kunzea ambigua
description: A hardy upright shrub with small heath-like leaves and masses of fluffy flowers in spring and summer. It makes a good screen and feeds bees and small birds.

name: Kunzea baxteri
description: A spreading shrub from the south coast of Western Australia with bright red bottlebrush flowers on and off for most of the year. Its fine leaves suit a screen or hedge.
pruning: It responds very well to pruning.

name: Melaleuca thymifolia
description: A small shrub with corky bark and small leaves that grows naturally in damp heath and at the edges of swamps. Its nectar-rich flowers attract birds and butterflies, and it makes a low hedge.
pruning: A light trim now and then keeps it dense.

name: Epacris longiflora
description: A small heath from sandy cliffs and heaths with long, tubular flowers through most of the year, fewer in summer. Small honeyeaters feed on them.
care_note: It likes well-drained, slightly acid, sandy soil with regular moisture.

name: Swainsona formosa
description: The floral emblem of South Australia: a sprawling plant with grey-green leaves and red flowers with glossy black centres. Some forms are cream, pink or red all over. It is an annual or a short-lived perennial.
care_note: It needs perfect drainage, full sun and very little water once the seedling is established.

name: Indigofera australis
description: A light, spreading shrub with spires of pink to purple pea flowers in spring. It is a good nectar plant for butterflies and copes with neglect, some frost and dry spells.
pruning: A light prune keeps it shapely.

name: Olearia phlogopappa
description: A small shrub with grey-green leaves that is covered in masses of small daisies from late spring to early autumn. It suits massed plantings, a low hedge or a pot.
pruning: Prune after flowering to keep it compact.

name: Ozothamnus diosmifolius
description: An upright shrub with aromatic, curry-scented leaves and dense clusters of tiny flowers from late winter to spring. The flowers are good fresh or dried.
pruning: Trim back after each flush of flowers to bring on more.

name: Acacia cultriformis
description: A shrub with silver-grey, knife-shaped leaves and clusters of golden ball flowers from late winter into spring. Wrens and thornbills hunt insects among the flowers, and prostrate forms such as 'Cascade' spill over walls and banks.
care_note: It has naturalised on parts of the New South Wales central and north coasts, outside its natural range.

name: Acacia cognata
description: A wattle with long, narrow, weeping leaves and small ball flowers from winter into spring. Compact forms such as 'Bower Beauty' are grown for their soft, graceful foliage.
care_note: It is prone to root rot in humid climates and does best in the southern states.

name: Brachychiton rupestris
description: A large tree whose trunk swells into a bottle shape after five to ten years and stores water. It drops its leaves before it flowers.

name: Syzygium paniculatum
description: A lilly pilly from coastal rainforest on the New South Wales central coast, with glossy leaves, pink new growth, white flowers in summer and edible magenta fruit. Compact forms such as 'Beachball' suit hedges and pots.

name: Eucalyptus leucoxylon
description: A spreading gum with smooth grey or yellowish bark and large flowers that vary from yellow to pink or dark red. It is widely planted in southern Australia but struggles in humid places such as Sydney and Brisbane.

name: Eucalyptus caesia
description: A small, weeping gum from granite outcrops in Western Australia, with red young stems, white branches and curling minni-ritchi bark. Large pink-red flowers with yellow stamens appear in winter and spring.

name: Eucalyptus erythrocorys
description: A small mallee gum from Western Australia's mid coast with bright red bud caps that open to large golden-yellow flowers in late summer and early autumn, followed by large ornamental gum nuts.
pruning: It responds well to pruning and can be kept to size.

name: Ptilotus exaltatus
description: A short-lived plant from arid Australia with feathery, cone-shaped pink to purple flower spikes from winter into summer. It makes a good cut flower.
care_note: It does best where summers are dry, in an open, sunny spot with excellent drainage.

name: Hibbertia pedunculata
description: A low, fine-leaved shrub, sometimes prostrate, with golden buttercup-like flowers mainly in spring and summer. It suits edging, pots and raised beds.
pruning: Light pruning after flowering makes it denser.

name: Brachyscome angustifolia
description: A native daisy that forms a soft, spreading mound and flowers through the warmer months, best in spring and autumn. Selections such as 'Brasco Violet' suit mass planting, rockeries and pots.
pruning: A light trim when it looks untidy is all it needs.

name: Lambertia formosa
description: A spreading shrub with prickly leaves and red tubular flowers, mainly in spring and summer. Its woody seed pods look like a little devil's face, and its nectar feeds honeyeaters.

name: Beaufortia sparsa
description: A shrub from the south-west of Western Australia with spectacular orange to red bottlebrush flower clusters in summer and into autumn. Birds visit the flowers, and it copes with both dry and moist soil.
pruning: Cutting flowers for a vase prunes it at the same time.
care_note: It can be short-lived in humid, high-rainfall areas and does best in drier climates.

name: Calothamnus quadrifidus
description: A tough shrub with fine leaves and red bottlebrush flowers held along one side of the stems in spring and summer. Honeyeaters feed on them, and it makes a good hedge.
pruning: A light trim keeps it compact and flowering well.

name: Hypocalymma angustifolium
description: A dainty shrub with narrow, spicy-scented leaves and masses of small pink and white flowers along the stems in late winter and spring. It grows naturally beside streams and swamps.
pruning: Prune after flowering to keep it dense.

name: Alyogyne hakeifolia
description: A long-flowering native hibiscus. Selections such as 'Elle Marie' have creamy yellow flowers with a red centre.
pruning: Prune after spring flowering to thicken the plant and bring on new flowering growth.

name: Hakea francisiana
description: An upright shrub with blue-green leaves and long pinkish-red flower spikes in winter and spring. In the eastern states it is often sold grafted, which helps it cope with heavier soil.
pruning: A light trim after flowering keeps it dense.

name: Actinotus helianthi
description: An iconic wildflower with soft, woolly leaves and felty flower heads, mainly in spring. Cutting the flowers for the house also prunes it.
care_note: It needs very good drainage, ideally sandy soil.

name: Dampiera diversifolia
description: A prostrate plant from southern Western Australia with bright blue to purple-blue flowers with pale centres in spring and summer. It spreads up to a metre across.

name: Tetratheca thymifolia
description: A small, multi-stemmed shrub with nodding pink to mauve bell flowers with dark centres, mostly in spring. It is tougher than it looks and makes a good pot plant.
pruning: Give it a light trim and a feed after flowering.

name: Westringia 'Glabra Cadabra'
description: A hardy westringia with soft grey-green leaves and mauve flowers, mainly in spring. It is very salt tolerant and responds well to pruning, so it suits hedges, screens and topiary.

name: Eustrephus latifolius
description: A twining vine with small, fringed white to pink flowers in spring and summer, and orange berries through winter that birds eat. It is not rampant and can also scramble as a groundcover.

name: Banksia spinulosa 'Birthday Candles'
description: A dense, compact form of the hairpin banksia with flower spikes in autumn and winter. It suits rockeries, small gardens and pots.
care_note: On heavy soil, please plant it in a raised bed with some organic matter.
